links.reason: Both set the scene at the Vaigai of Koodal, and Paripadal 10.23 does list பதிவத மாதர், பரத்தையர் in one crowd. But Akananuru 296 makes the bathing itself part of the charge (இன்றும் பெருநீர் வையை அவளொடு ஆடி, புலரா மார்பினை), so 'cannot be the bathing itself' and 'licensed public pleasure' go beyond what either poem says.

The venba's என்மனைக்கு ஏறக்கொணருமோ ... தன்மனைக்கே உய்க்குமோ repeats Akananuru 195's எம்மனை முந்துறத் தருமோ? தன்மனை உய்க்குமோ? almost word for word, addressed to one who tells by his god. The short poem drops the rival mother's preparations and the nursing (கூந்தல் வாரி, நுசுப்பு இவர்ந்து), so the teaches claim about a fixed question that stands alone is borne out.

Kuruntokai 32 says only that proclaiming on the madal is பழி and living apart is பழி; it does not say on whom the blame falls, so the note's 'blame for the man' is supplied. Kalittokai 58's நீ படு பழியே assigns it to her, which extends rather than contradicts the shorter poem.

The shared figure is exact: வலன்ஏர்ப்பு in Ainkurunuru 469 and வைகலும் ஏரும் வலம் in Kar Narpathu 12, both spoken by the friend to steady the heroine. The contrast of proof (ஐயந்தீர் காட்சி) and escort (தரீஇய, காண்குவம் வம்மோ) is true but slight; this is a shared omen more than a development.

Patitruppattu 26's நோகோ யானே is the poet's open grief over the ravaged land. Purananuru 25's turn, சிதைதல் உய்ந்தன்றோ நின்வேல், need not mean the king's restraint (it can mean the spear escaped damage), so the 'hoped-for restraint' half of the teaches rests on a contested reading and the rest is the shared topic of war's ruin.

The link is the word மருள்மாலை: in the venba the evening is செயவர் செய்த குறி, in the Kural a fellow sufferer (புன்கண்ணை, வன்கண்ணதோ நின் துணை). These are different speakers in different situations, which the brief says is not tension, and 'meaning depends on who speaks' restates the convention. The venba's speaker is itself inferred.

பெட்பின்றி ஈதல் யாம்வேண்டலமே answers directly to இகழ்ந்தெள்ளாது ஈவாரை: both measure the manner of giving. The pairing shows something neither shows alone, that what the Kural states as the receiver's inner joy (உள்ளுள் உவப்பது) the bard turns into a condition he states before praise.

Both oodal scenes turn on the man and birds: Kalittokai 95's குறும்பூழ் போர் alibi and Paripadal 18's மஞ்ஞை and களி மகிழ் பேதுற்ற இதல். But in the Paripadal the gaze is not an excuse for absence or another woman; he explains it as thought of her (நின் இயல் களவு), and இதல் is not the same bird-word as பூழ், so 'the same excuse of bird-watching' overstates it.

Akananuru 388 quotes the hunter's question (புண்கூர்ந்து எவ்வமொடு வந்த உயர்மருப்பு ஒருத்தல் நும் புனத்துழிப் போகல் உறுமோ) and Thinaimozhi 8 is a bare answer (சோர்ந்து குருதி ஒழுக ... போந்ததுஇல் ஐய! களிறு). The short verse is legible only as the reply to that fixed pretext, which is what the teaches says.

மருந்து பிறிது இன்மை in Natrinai 247 turns Kural 1102's தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து onto the man, and the thurai நீட்டியாமை வரை places it as the friend pressing for marriage. The reversal of who is the cure, and its use as argument, is specific and true.

Both use the eye-like-flower convention: Kural 1112's பலர்காணும் பூவொக்கும் is rejected as unworthy, Kalittokai 45's மலர் ஏய்க்கும் என்பதோ is ironic accusation. These are not incompatible claims about one thing but two uses of a figure, so the type is wrong, though the contrast in the teaches is real.

Kuruntokai 243's உள்ளேன் தோழி படீஇயர்என் கண்ணே is a vow not to think, and Kural 1207 says மறப்பறியேன், உள்ளினும் உள்ளம் சுடும். The teaches reading (the need to vow confirms remembering keeps her awake) is fair, but neither verse limits the other; it applies the couplet's bind to a case.

Kuruntokai 65's இரலை தன் இன்புறு துணையொடு frisks as if asking the waiting women இருந்திரோ, while Ainkurunuru 419's beasts புணர்ந்தன நம்போல் in a decade of the returned man's praise of the season. The same paired beasts in rain are reproach before return and mirror after it, which the teaches states accurately.

The two share a structure: புலவியஃது எவனோ அன்பிலங் கடையே and நோதல் எவன் ... காதலர் இல்லா வழி. Kuruntokai 93 adds அன்னையும் அத்தனும் அல்லரோ, her dependence, as the reason she will not let him be blamed, so the pair shows the maxim applied and ending in silence.

கல்லினும் வலியன் ... வலியன் என்னாது மெலியும் என் நெஞ்சே sets the man's hardness against her own heart's softness, and Kural 1291 asks the heart why it is not hers when his is his (அவர்நெஞ்சு அவர்க்காதல்). Both make the heart, not the man, the object of complaint, and the image/argument division is fair.

The identification is secure: மூவகை ஆர் எயில் and உமையொடு புணர்ந்து in Paripadal 5 match மூவெயில் முருக்கிய and உமையமர்ந்து விளங்கும் இமையா முக்கண் in the guide poem. The teaches point (narrated in one, epithet in the other) is true but generic to the genres, and it leans on line 256, which the packet does not show.

Both are the stock mullai moment: the season's signs come (சேர்ந்தன செய்குறி; கார்தோன்ற) and he does not, and pallor follows (கூர்ந்த பசலை; பீர்தோன்றி). The 'diagnosis vs accusation' contrast rests on calling the venba's speaker the woman, which the verse does not state, though சொற்பழுதால் does lay blame.

241 asks of the velan கேண்மை அறியுமோ தில்ல; 249 blesses him (வாழிய) because he is நாடனை அறியாதோன். Within one decade the diviner's ignorance moves from doubt to the secret's safety, which is a real development the teaches names correctly.

Ainkurunuru 65's புதல்வனை ஈன்றஎம் மேனி ... நின் மார்புசிதைப்பதுவே and Natrinai 380's நெய்யும் குய்யும் ... புனிறு நாறும் ... தேரோற்கு ஒத்தனெம் அல்லேம் make the same refusal from the body of a nursing mother. Natrinai sets the marks against வால் இழை மகளிர் சேரி, which is what the sarcastic short phrase implies.

Kural 1151 refuses the promise of வல்வரவு in words; in Kuruntokai 256 the promise (வருதும் ... தாங்கல் ஒல்லுமோ) is cut off சொல்லா முன்னர் by her tears, which தேர்விலங்கின. The contrast of spoken and wordless refusal is specific; 'it worked' slightly overstates விலங்கின, which says the eyes blocked the chariot.

Natrinai 284's உடம்பு is a தேய்புரிப் பழங் கயிறு seized at both ends by tuskers (heart vs அறிவு); Kural 1163's உயிர் is the pole (காவாத் தூங்கும்) for காமமும் நாணும் in a நோனா உடம்பு. One figure of a body strained between two claims, used for the man's and the woman's conflicts, as the teaches says.

The verbal link is exact: அஞ்சல் ஓம்பு and தெளி in Kalittokai 132, அளித்தஞ்சல் and தெளித்தசொல் in Kural 1154. The poem turns each reassurance into பயன், சிறப்பு, கொளை of a named loss, giving the couplet's question of fault a speech situation, as the teaches says.

Perumpanatruppadai's herd girl sells அளை for food but நெய்விலைக் கட்டிப் பசும்பொன் கொள்ளாள், taking cattle; Kalittokai 110's girl rebukes the man who thinks அளைக்கு எளியாள் வெண்ணெய்க்கும் அன்னள். The idyll's price difference is what gives the retort its edge; வெண்ணெய் vs நெய் is close enough.

Both have the girls guarding drying fish (பல்மீன் உணங்கல் படுபுள் ஓப்புதும்; மீன் ... பார்த்தும் பகர்தும்). The teaches rests on Natrinai 45, a third poem outside the pair, and concludes only that the venba's sense 'stays open', which is not something the pair teaches.

Paripadal 13 orders விசும்பு, வளி, தீ, நீர் by the number of senses that know each; Tirumanthiram 385's chain வான், வாயு, கான், நீர், கடினம் would put கான் in fire's slot. That supports reading கான் as fire only as the standard element order does anywhere, and the Paripadal gives a theory of knowing, not of emergence, so 'the creation chain ... already present' overstates it.

The figure is distinctive and shared: காயா அஞ்சன மலர in Mullaippattu 93 and கண்ணியல் அஞ்சனம் தோய்ந்தபோல் காயாவும் in Kar Narpathu 8. In the venba the friend points to it as sign of return; in the idyll it lines the road the returning chariot runs, a true and specific difference.

Paripadal 9.81 கற்பு இணை நெறியூடு அற்பு இணைக் கிழமை plausibly names the god's two unions, and the guide poem gives a face to வள்ளியொடு நகையமர்ந்தன்றே. The teaches is reasonable, but the guide poem's 'chaste wife' epithet is outside the lines shown, and reading line 81 as the two consorts needs the rest of Paripadal 9.

Akananuru 74 blames the instrument, கல்லாக் கோவலர் ஊதும் வல்வாய் சிறுகுழல், while Ainthinai 7 grants the flute is சீர்சால் and the herdsman plays உவந்து, yet வேல்கொண்டு எறிவது போலும். The pain shifts from the sound to the hearer, which the teaches states, and the venba does qualify the Akananuru's blame.

The shared thing is the sand doll: வண்டற் பாவை in Ainkurunuru 124, திணிமணல் செய்வுறு பாவை in Purananuru 243. The nostalgia/contempt contrast is real, but the note's 'leaps into water' is only in the puram poem, and the pair shares an image rather than one qualifying the other.

Paripadal 2's இளையன் என்போர்க்கு இளையை ... முதியை என்போர்க்கு முதுமை is a rank given by the worshipper; Paripadal 4 extends it to வேறு வேறு பெயரோய், தொழுத கை அமைதியின் அமர்ந்தோய், and அவரவர் ஏவலாளனும் நீயே. The widening from rank to name, place and service is in the Tamil.

Both name the man's heroic motive (Kural உரன்நசைஇ; Kar Narpathu நச்சியார்க்கு ஈதலும் நண்ணார்த் தெறுதலும்). But the Kural verse states her living on longing (வரல்நசைஇ இன்னும் உளேன்), not a grievance, and in Kar Narpathu the guarantee is the rain (தரூஉம் ... மழை), not the motive.

Both show the husband approaching through the son (Kainnilai கட்டலர் கண்ணிப் புதல்வனைக் கொண்டு ... சுட்டி அலைய வரும்; Natrinai புதல்வன் ... முயங்கல் விருப்பொடு குறுகினேம்). They are two poems of one stock situation from two speakers, not incompatible claims about one event, so this is not a tension; the teaches treats them as one scene.

The anklet is shared: மெல்லடி மேலவும் சிலம்பே in Kuruntokai 7, தெரிசிலம்பு கழீஇ in Akananuru 321. But Kuruntokai 7's onlookers judge only அளியர்; that they read the anklet as the sign of an unwed girl in flight is supplied from tradition, not said in the poem.

Akananuru 222 names ஆதி மந்தி and ஆட்டன் அத்தி; Kuruntokai 31 names no one, and the identification rests on the colophon's poet ஆதிமந்தியார். The ஆடுகள மகன் of 31 fits the dancer of 222, but 'the legend outlived the poet's lament' is not something the pair shows.

Akananuru 144 has the man imagine her charge (கதுப்பும் உள்ளார், அறன்அஞ்சலரே) and Ainkurunuru 484 has him confess it (நீடினம் நேரிழை மறந்தே) while urging the charioteer (கடியக் கடவுமதி பாக). The reversal of reproach into self-accusation is specific and accurate.

Kar Narpathu 11's அணர்த்தெழு பாம்பின் தலைபோல் கோடல் is the hood stage read as promise; Thinaimalai 119 follows the same flower through துடுப்பாய் பாம்பாய் விரலாய் ... வெண்குடையாம் to வீந்து. The flower-as-calendar reading is in the Tamil, though line 1 of the venba is obscure.

Ainkurunuru 18 quotes his promise against him (பிரிந்தனன் அல்லனோ பிரியலென் என்றே); Kural 1154 asks whether தேறியார் are at fault when he who said அஞ்சல் leaves. The couplet adds the question of the believer's blame, which the poem does not raise.

The link rests on the colophon naming கோப்பெருஞ்சோழன் for both, and on புலவர் தோழ, which in Kuruntokai 129 is an address to the comrade, not to a poet-friend of the king. Purananuru 216 never names a poet; turning the akam paangan into a real friendship of poets is biography read into the poems.

Both are the kurinji end of the field season: Natrinai 259's புலர் பதம் கொண்டன ஏனற் குரலே, Ainthinai 11's போயின சின்னாள் புனத்து. The added point, ஏயினார் இன்றி as what made the days sweet, is true, but this is a stock situation and the pair adds little beyond it.

Kurinjippattu 175-177 (நெடுவேள் அணங்குறு மகளிர் ஆடுகளம் கடுப்பத் திணிநிலைக் கடம்பின்) and the guide poem's வெறியயர் களனும் ... புதுப்பூங் கடம்பும் share the kadamba and veri ground. But the teaches' point (the mother's suspected seizure returning as simile) is internal to Kurinjippattu; the guide poem's list adds nothing to it.

The two similes are built alike: பிரிந்தவர் மேனிபோல் புல்லென்ற வள்ளி பொருந்தினர் மேனிபோல் பொற்ப and செல்வர் மனம்போற் கவினீன்ற நல்கூர்ந்தார் மேனிபோற் புல்லென்ற காடு. One measures the revival by wealth and poverty, the other by parting and union, which is a specific and true contrast.

மனைக்குவிளக் காயினள் ... புதல்வன் தாயே and குடிக்குவிளக்கு ஆகிய புதல்வற் பயந்த share the title and its ground in bearing a son. Akananuru adds கடவுட் கற்பு, Ainkurunuru the literal பாண்டில் செஞ்சுடர், as the teaches says.

Kurinjippattu's simile இகன்மீக் கடவும் இருபெரு வேந்தர் வினையிடை நின்ற சான்றோர் போல names exactly the position Kovur Kizhar takes in Purananuru 45 (ஒருவீர் தோற்பினும் தோற்ப நும் குடியே). The puram poem shows from inside why the go-between's இருபேர் அச்சம் has no safe side.

Kural 548 says the king who does not ஓரா முறைசெய் perishes தானே; the Pandya says யானோ அரசன் யானே கள்வன் ... கெடுகவென் ஆயுள் and falls, naming only his heeding of the goldsmith (பொன்செய் கொல்லன் தன்சொற் கேட்ட). The self-sentence makes 'by himself' literal, as the teaches says.

poems.note: The breeze-stirred grove 'telling' the girl is the season's sign, not an act a person of the situation does.
The thazhai is joined to the man by அருளாதவர் போல், an open comparison.
Anchor is thin: the straying is implied by the town's talk, not stated; pairs are the narai as the man, the heron's chick as the other house's child, and resting in the grove as his staying away.
The jasmine buds as teeth make the season laugh; that is a look read as mockery, not a deed of the situation.

iraicchi.act: the tusker strips the yaa bark to ease its she-elephant's hunger
iraicchi.sense: the man who passes such tender acts on his road will be moved to care for her and return.

ullurai.anchor: துஞ்சாக் காவலர் இகழ் பதம் நோக்கி இரவின் வரூஉம்

poems.note: Boar slipping into the guarded field = the man coming by night; the lizard's warning = the sleepless guards; its slow retreat to its lair = the withdrawal the friend urges.
Hard to apply: the startled monkey as the man and the hunter's drawn bow as the town's gossip fit, but the heroine insists he is unchanged, so the mapping is contested.
மீனெறி தூண்டிலின் is an open simile but only for the bamboo; the elephant scared by the millet guards and letting go the bamboo maps to the man kept off and her springing back bereft.
Lines 1-2 are obscure and the creature is unnamed, so no two correspondences can be fixed.
The water-rooted kuvalai that summer cannot wither pairs well with her safe beside him, but it is a water flower used by the friend in a paalai poem.
The spring scene is built of open similes (போல்) and states its own sense (வாரார் தோழி).

ullurai.anchor: குன்ற நாடன் கேண்மை மென்தோள் சாய்த்துஞ் சால்பீன் றன்றே

poems.note: The ripe fruit loosed by the monkey's touch and carried to the common drinking ford maps to the love the man began being brought into the open toward honour; the second pair is interpretive.

iraicchi.act: the red dog watches for a boar to feed its craving mate
iraicchi.sense: the sight of a mate providing for its own turns the man's heart back to the woman he loves.

iraicchi.act: the tethered calf frets for its absent mother and is told she will come now
iraicchi.sense: like the calf, the waiting wife will soon have the one she waits for.

poems.note: The calf works inside a virichi omen; the iraicchi and the omen overlap.

iraicchi.act: the vulture cock, hearing the drum, goes back to its flock
iraicchi.sense: even the bird turns home to its own, so the man should give up the journey and stay with her.

poems.note: The vulture belongs to the danger description; the iraicchi reading follows the thurai செலவு அழுங்கியது.

carrier: தன் துணை பிரிந்து அயாஅம் தனி குருகு
iraicchi.act: the lone heron parted from its mate grieves and keeps her company in the night
iraicchi.sense: her lying alone is a parted pair's grief, which only his return can end.

poems.note: The heron is named as her துணை openly, so the sense is half stated.
